sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6 retrieved; section 6.2.1, equations 6.511–6.523, read in full.

contents.name: Section 6.2.1, free Coulomb-gauge modes and the two transverse polarization states, equations 6.511–6.514
contents.support: The notes derive the momentum-space constraint ξ·p=0 and identify a two-dimensional transverse plane at each nonzero momentum. The local definition states the complex fiber, its helicity projections, measure, and Hilbert pairing explicitly.

contents.name: Section 6.2.1, constrained commutator and transverse projector, equations 6.515–6.523
contents.support: The notes give the projector δij−pi pj/|p|² as the completeness sum for two transverse polarizations. The local proof verifies the same projection and its helicity splitting.

sources.title: Eric Palmerduca and Hong Qin, Photon topology, arXiv:2308.11147v2
sources.locator: Full 66-page PDF retrieved; section II, equations 5–15 and section III, definition 14, lemma 15, theorem 18, and equations 59–63. The total-bundle discussion and the complete Chern-curvature calculation were inspected.

contents.name: Section II, photon bundle over the punctured light cone and mass-shell measure, equations 5–15
contents.support: The paper uses d³k/(2|k|) and describes the transverse photon fiber. The local lemma proves the precise isometry to the published d³k transverse space, including the radial multiplier and equivalence of null sets.

contents.name: Section III, definition 14 and lemma 15, circularly polarized helicity line subbundles
contents.support: The paper defines the two circular-polarization line fibers inside the rank-two transverse bundle. The local definition constructs them as the ranges of the smooth projectors Pσ=(P+σh)/2.

contents.name: Section III, theorem 18 and equations 59–63, Berry curvature and the nonzero first Chern numbers
contents.support: The paper computes opposite helicity Chern numbers of magnitude two from the local polarization connection and explains the absence of global continuous unit helicity vectors. Its skew-Hermitian connection convention gives c1=−2σ for the local σ labels used here; the local proof also records the design's real Berry-flux convention, whose normalized flux is +2σ.

contents.name: Section III, consequence of theorem 18: no continuous global unit circular-helicity vector
contents.support: The source derives the global-frame obstruction from nonzero Chern number. The local counterexample separately checks the constant Cartesian vector at k=κe1 and does not infer that every abstract Hilbert-space tensor decomposition is impossible.

sources.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
sources.locator: Full 8-page PDF retrieved; section I, equation 1 and transversality discussion; section II, equations 6–9 on the helicity basis and Berry connection. The source uses hbar=c=1.

contents.name: Section I, equation 1 and adjacent transversality discussion, total angular momentum L+S
contents.support: The paper records the momentum-space vector rotation generator and warns that separate orbital and spin components need not preserve transversality. The local theorem derives the generator from U(R) and uses Stone's theorem for self-adjointness.

contents.name: Section II, equations 6–9, helicity basis and Berry gauge connection
contents.support: The source computes the helicity Berry connection in a momentum-dependent gauge and notes its monopole curvature. Its gauge and Chern sign conventions are recorded separately from the explicit Chern-Weil convention in the local proposition.

contents.name: Section II, momentum-dependent helicity basis and transverse projection
contents.support: The source expresses circular polarizations in a local spherical frame. The local definition makes the frame-independent projectors primary and supplies the Hilbert-space and bundle domains.
